scope: Source-by-source review. Direct primary-text checks are distinguished from publication metadata and corroboration. No source PDFs are redistributed in this repository.

references.exact_constant_audit: verification/audit_cubic_literature.py independently checks the coarse decimal constants in Lemma 5.1 by rational powers and a positive exponential series, and checks the Chebyshev/Joukowski Laurent identities and final strict sign. The branch and integral arguments were checked from the primary text.

references.citation: Manuscripta Math. 112 (2003), no. 4, 519--538.
references.verification: Primary author PDF read and DOI metadata checked.
references.pages: Theorem 1 and Corollary 1 pp. 521--522; Theorem 4 pp. 535--536.
references.use: Laplace representation/logarithmic convexity in the history; exterior square-root derivative Parseval formula in the proof. Passage to a critical level is justified by length continuity and increasing nonnegative coefficient sums. No Jordan-curve assumption is imposed on a critical boundary.
references.critical_level_correction: The prose on p. 536 says the curve is homeomorphic to a circle at the critical level and that its length is decreasing above that level. Neither assertion can be used literally: z^n-1 has a multiple-point boundary, and z^n has length 2 pi exp(t/n), which increases. The representation itself is correct. The manuscript uses the regular level r>1, divides its length by r, and lets r decrease to one using coefficient-sum monotonicity and continuity of L(r^(-n)p(rz)). This independently justifies the critical-level formula.

references.author: A. B. Olde Daalhuis
references.citation: Hypergeometric function, Chapter 15 in NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions.
references.verification: Primary connection formula and its local solution definitions checked.
references.use: Specialization A=B=(1+x)/2, C=1, 0<x<1. The exponent difference at unity is -x, not an integer. The singular coefficient is 2^x B(1/2,x/2), the constant is 2 pi Gamma(-x)/Gamma((1-x)/2)^2, and the error is O((1-u)^(1-x)). Equality A=B does not invalidate the zero-to-one connection formula.

Its small-curvature argument uses singular windows and a resultant, while the present common curvature estimate uses the transported square-root derivative and signed Laurent kernels. The shared elementary quartic critical-value difference is obtained directly by integration in each source.

references.citation: The maximal length of the Erdos--Herzog--Piranian lemniscate in high degree, arXiv:2512.12455v2 [math.CV] (2025).
references.verification: Primary fifty-six-page v2 read; version revised 22 December 2025. Statements and normalizations checked against the displayed equations.

references.citation: C. Wang and L. Peng, The arc length of the lemniscate |w^n+c|=1, Rocky Mountain J. Math. 36 (2006), no. 1, 337--347.
references.verification: Author, title, DOI, volume, issue and pages verified in the publisher DOI metadata and journal issue contents. Danchenko p. 1117 also cites this exact item. The full original article was not accessible from Project Euclid during this audit.
references.use: Historical attribution of the extremal comparison within the one-critical-value family, not an imported proof lemma. The comparison is independently checked below.
references.independent_check: For n>1 put b=(1-1/n)/2. The inverse arclength integral for z^n+c is the circle mean of |e^(it)-c|^(-2b). For 0<=r=|c|<1 it equals 2 pi sum_j ((b)_j/j!)^2 r^(2j), which is increasing. At r=1 the integral is finite and the limit follows from the integrable bound given by (1-r)^2+r|1-e^(it)|^2. For r>1 it is r^(-2b) times its value at 1/r, hence strictly smaller than at 1. For n=1 every value is 2 pi.

independent_arc_capacity_check.verification: The pole -s is inside the unit disk. On |w|=1 the image is exp(2 i arg(1+s w)), hence the closed arc |arg z|<=alpha. The only critical points are -s +/- i sqrt(1-s^2), on the unit circle, and their images are the endpoints. For a large target value exactly one inverse root lies outside the unit disk. This number is unchanged throughout the connected complement of the arc because a root can cross the unit circle only above the arc. Thus Psi maps the exterior disk conformally onto the arc complement. Its leading coefficient at infinity is s, so capacity is s.

excluded_claims.claim: A certified general finite range n<=14 in the Mendoza experiments.
excluded_claims.finding: The current README and the author correction withdraw proof-level certification. The work sampled a bounded coefficient box, omitted the model-containing half for n>=6, and used floating contours and an unproved Lipschitz estimate. It is not cited as an established finite-degree theorem.
excluded_claims.pr_status: Closed, not merged; the finite-range sibling was removed. A Lean statement with sorry is not a formal proof.

writing_sources.applied: Accurate result statements, notation aligned with the source problem, explicit dependency lemmas, and enough detail at limiting and computational steps. The introduction was lightly edited, not replaced by a new historical narrative.
writing_sources.final_pass_application: Global disk norms are defined before use and are distinguished from circle L2 norms. Reused proof constructions are identified explicitly. The second constant coefficient is obtained from one universal extraction identity and two affine identities. The conditional proof graph is recorded separately and checked for cycles. Computational success is not presented as a proof of the connecting analytic statements.

independent_area_normalization_check: For a normalized univalent exterior map f(w)=w+a0+sum a_j w^(-j), Green's formula on |w|=r>1 gives area of its bounded complement equal to pi(r^2-sum j |a_j|^2 r^(-2j)). This area is nonnegative. Letting r decrease to one proves the exterior area inequality in the stated normalization; translation a0 contributes zero.

additional_literature_considered.status: Publisher and author-institution metadata checked. Full original scan was not accessible through the attempted archive. Not imported as a proof lemma and not added to the bibliography merely on a title/metadata match.
additional_literature_considered.comparison: The elementary compactness statement is the properness property of the polynomial critical-value map. Its short coefficient-normalization proof is retained, so no stronger singularity-theoretic covering theorem is required.
